## The Core Claim

Maxwell's equations predict a fixed speed for electromagnetic waves in vacuum, independent of any reference frame -- a result inconsistent with classical Galilean addition of velocities. Einstein (1905) resolved this by rejecting Galilean relativity's assumption of absolute simultaneity, deriving instead that space and time measurements are frame-dependent (time dilation, length contraction) in exactly the way needed to keep Maxwell's equations form-invariant across all inertial frames -- special relativity was built directly from taking Maxwell's electromagnetism at face value rather than amending it. NOTE, disclosed: Einstein's 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics was for the photoelectric effect, not for relativity; the relativity-from-Maxwell derivation is real, foundational, essentially universally accepted physics, but -- like Feynman's case above -- is not itself the cited Nobel-winning work.
